name: Tarocchi Bolognesi
description: Tarocchi Bolognesi (or Tarocchino Bolognese) refers to the family of games played with the specific 62-card Tarot deck from Bologna. The most common variant is Ottocento, but the term covers the deck and system itself. The deck removes ranks 2-5 from each suit of a standard Tarot pack.
duration: Typically 30–60 minutes per session depending on variant and number of deals.

overview.description: Tarocchi Bolognesi (or Tarocchino Bolognese) refers to the family of games played with the specific 62-card Tarot deck from Bologna. The most common variant is Ottocento, but the term covers the deck and system itself. The deck removes ranks 2-5 from each suit of a standard Tarot pack.

history.origins: The Tarocco Bolognese is one of the oldest tarot decks in continual use. Tarocchi were mentioned in connection with Bologna by 1442 and in Bologna itself by 1459. The deck was reduced from 78 to 62 cards during the 16th century by removing ranks 2 to 5 from each suit; in 1725 the imperial and papal trumps were converted to four Moors. The deck and its games have historically been confined to Bologna.
timeline: Early 16th century: Deck reduced from 78 to 62 cards by removing ranks 2–5.
1725: Imperial and papal trumps converted to four Moors (Moretti) in Bolognese deck.
history.evolution: Ottocento became the dominant game, but others like Terziglio exist.

setup.players: Two to six depending on variant; Ottocento (the main game) is for four players in fixed partnerships, two against two.
setup.deck: 62 cards: Trumps 0-20 + Matto. 4 Suits (10 cards each).

rules.objective: In the main variant Ottocento, the objective is to score points from card values and declared combinations; the first partnership to reach 800 points wins the rubber. Other variants (e.g. Terziglio, Millone) have their own targets.
